_comment: COUPLING tier-2, the fixture that justifies every other one asserting a closed form instead of `converged`. Runs the SAME coupling twice, changing exactly one constant: the right subdomain's outer boundary temperature, written once in kelvin and once as the same physical temperature in degrees Celsius. `couple` cannot tell them apart — both converge in a comparable number of iterations to a comparable residual, both have an EMPTY validation block, and both balance the interface flux to roundoff (the mismatched run balanced BETTER than the correct one, because conservation is a property of the fixed point and holds whatever units the boundary data is in). The difference is visible only against an independent answer, and it is not subtle: the interface temperature is out by tens of percent and the flux by an order of magnitude. Then check_monolithic_consistency is run explicitly on both, and fires on exactly one. The control run is the built-in mutation: remove the unit mismatch and the 'disagrees with the closed form' assertions fail.
